sources: Fri Aug 28 2026 run, executed 06:15 UTC / 02:15 ET - BEFORE the US cash open and BEFORE today's 10:00 ET UMich final, so the last complete session on the board is Thursday Aug 27. THEME: vol collapsed across assets while credit tightened and freight kept bleeding - a risk-ON week on every market-priced gauge, with the soft spots confined to the survey/consumer data. CRUDE STABILISED AFTER A FOUR-DAY UNWIND: Brent 88.22 (TradingEconomics Aug 28 CFD print, -0.34% d/d; live quote 88.30, Aug 27 close 88.52), UP from 87.11 in yesterday's file but DOWN on the week from ~92-94 around Aug 21. Wednesday's slide reversed Thursday on Russia-Ukraine escalation (Putin said talks yielded nothing and Russia was preparing to intensify; Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries and ports are constraining export capacity), then eased again Friday. Goldman says Persian Gulf exports have recovered to ~2/3 of pre-war levels, 15-16mb/d, still 7-8mb/d below pre-conflict but well above the 5-6mb/d March trough. Iran-Oman revenue-sharing deal on Hormuz stands but Tehran repeats it does not guarantee reopening; the Trump administration told mediators it has no interest in reviving the collapsed June preliminary deal. WTI 83.17. Heating oil 4.30 (+0.50%) and gasoline 3.38 - downstream tightness STILL unresolved, heating oil +89% y/y. VOL BROKE LOWER ON BOTH LEGS: VIX 14.51 Aug 27 close (-0.70 d/d from 15.21), DOWN from 16.01 a week earlier - back toward the 2026 low (14.25 on Aug 14). MOVE 69.86 Aug 27 (ICE/BofAML via MacroMicro), DOWN from 73.18 a week ago and below the 70 handle for the first time since mid-August; note the '73, 54th percentile' figure carried in prior runs was the Aug 21 close, and Cboe has not published a percentile for the new print. Equity and rates vol falling together is the cleanest bullish tell on the board. CURVE - OFFICIAL SERIES NOW BACK: 10Y-2Y +0.47 (FRED T10Y2Y, Aug 27), not a derivation this time. FRED has caught up through Aug 27, so yesterday's inferred 0.43 was too flat - the true path was 0.50 (Aug 21) to 0.46 (Aug 24) to 0.47 (Aug 25-27). Still a w/w flattening of 3bp, still driven by the front end: 2Y 4.216% (TE Aug 27, -0.6bp d/d, -7.5bp on the month) against 10Y 4.65-4.68%. CREDIT TIGHTENED, REVERSING YESTERDAY'S WIDENING: HY OAS 267bp (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2, Aug 26 - the series runs one day in arrears, so Aug 27 lands with this morning's update), DOWN from 273 in yesterday's file and from 270 on Aug 21. That puts spreads back at the Aug 14 low. The two-way widening flagged yesterday did not extend; credit remains the cleanest place a real crack would show and it is not showing one. BREAKEVENS DRIFTED UP: T5YIFR 2.35% (FRED, Aug 27), UP from 2.33 and 2.34 a week ago - inflation expectations firming slightly even as crude sits below last week's level, which again argues the oil move is risk-premium unwind rather than demand destruction. DOLLAR FLAT-TO-SOFTER: DXY 99.187 (TE Aug 28, +0.05% d/d), essentially unchanged d/d but DOWN from ~99.80 a week ago. EUR/USD 1.1645, USD/JPY 159.54. GROWTH MIX STILL DEFENSIVE BUT LESS SO: gold 4,574.34 (-0.57%, off from 4,604 yesterday), copper 6.5945 (+0.08%). Copper/gold 1.44, UP from 1.43 as gold gave ground, but still DOWN from ~1.50 a week ago. Gold coming off is the first crack in the defensive bid. FREIGHT - FIFTH STRAIGHT DECLINE: BDTI 2,801 Aug 27 (StockQ, -1.75% d/d), DOWN from 2,851 and from 2,966 a week ago; the index topped at 3,004 on Aug 21 and has fallen every session since. YTD still +112%, so this remains the deepest red on the board, but the direction of travel is now unambiguously lower. MA5 2900.60, MA20 2747.70 - the 5-day is about to cross the 20-day from above. LABOUR HELD: initial claims 203k for week ending Aug 22 (DOL, released Aug 27), DOWN 4k and BELOW the ~208k consensus; prior week revised up to 207k, 4-week average 205.5k. Unadjusted claims 169,786 vs 191,208 in the comparable 2025 week. Employers are still not firing. FINANCIAL CONDITIONS - NEW PRINT: NFCI -0.566 for week ending Aug 21 (Chicago Fed/FRED, released Aug 26), marginally LOOSER than -0.561 the prior week. Loosest reading of the recent run. CARRIED, NO NEW PRINT: EUR/USD 3M xccy -10bp (no free dated quote; no funding-stress event in the window). SOFR-OIS ~2bp. Building permits 1,443k July SAAR. LEI y/y ~-1.1%. ISM Manufacturing 55.6 July (four-year high); August prints Sep 1. Sahm Rule -0.03 July; August prints Sep 4. UMich 51.0 August PRELIMINARY - the FINAL LANDS AT 10:00 ET TODAY and is NOT in this file; the preliminary was a 7.6% m/m collapse from 55.2 with expected business conditions down 11% short-run and 17% long-run, so the revision is the single most informative number of the day. Global liquidity 1=stable: Fed ended QT Dec 2025, ECB still shrinking through 2026 - divergent, net neutral. NET READ: nine of the ten market-priced series improved or held this week (vol both legs, credit, dollar, claims, financial conditions); the deterioration is entirely in freight, the flattening front end, and the consumer survey. WATCH: UMich final 10:00 ET today, PCE, ISM Sep 1, payrolls Sep 4, whether BDTI's 5-day breaks the 20-day, and whether HY OAS confirms 267 on today's update.
